newsitem.title: USA: Ford's Hertz unit Q1 net rises to $19.7 mln.
newsitem.headline: Ford's Hertz unit Q1 net rises to $19.7 mln.

text.p: Hertz Corp, Ford Motor Co's car rental unit, said Thursday it posted record earnings of $19.7 million in the first quarter of 1997, more than double the $8.8 million earned in the same period last year.
The increase was primarily due to higher revenues in its U.S. car rental operations, it said.
The company said it also achieved record revenues of $878.4 million in the first quarter, up $75.3 million from the same period last year.
It said revenues from car rental operations of $758.5 million rose by $67.8 million, as the number of transactdions and revenue per transaction increased, mainly in the U.S.

Revenues from its other business, industrial and construction equipment rental, increased by $13.3 million to $90.4 million, as volume rose from the opening of new locations and increased activity in industrial markets, it said.

Revenues from all other sources dropped by $5.8 million to $29.5 million due to lower revenues in claim administration service operations, a large part of which were sold in February 1996, it said. It noted that the decline was partly offset by revenues contributed by an acquisition of a foreign licensee operation in June 1996.

The company said its higher net earnings was partly offset by an $800,000 charge for the interest expense, net of taxes, relating to funding a $460 million dividend paid by the company to Ford in the first quarter and other items relating to the company's potential initial public offering.

Also partly offsetting earnings were increased costs in the industrial and contruction equipment rental business relating to the additional depreciation for equipment purchased and other expenses related to service new industrial customers.
It said it also incurred losses arising from its 1996 foreign car rental acquisition.
